summary: Silicon Valley Bank’s former parent company will not get $1.7 billion from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp., a federal judge ruled, because some executives made decisions that led to SVB’s bankruptcy.
content: A federal judge has ruled that Silicon Valley Bank’s former parent company is not entitled to recover $1.7 billion from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. The court determined that decisions made by certain executives directly contributed to the bank's bankruptcy, leading to the denial of the funds.

summary:

The post AI Opens a New Distribution Channel for Credit appeared first on PYMNTS.com.
content: Economic pressures are driving consumers to increasingly compare purchase costs, financing options, and alternatives before making buying decisions. In response, financial providers are integrating these financial choices directly into artificial intelligence platforms that consumers use for product research. This emerging trend establishes AI as a powerful new distribution channel for credit and financial products, reshaping how providers reach consumers during the research phase.
